item.title: Retailers adapt to rising AI shopping and the emergence of Muse agents
item.description:
Retailers adapt to rising AI shopping and the emergence of Muse agents

The Vergecast highlighted a recent surge in AI‑driven shopping and how it is pushing retailers to rethink customer interactions, now referred to as Muse agents.

🔍 Overview

  • An “ongoing increase in AI shopping” is shaping how retailers operate online.
  • The hosts framed this shift as a core issue for the future of the web, AI, and everything.

🛒 Impact on Retailers

  • Retailers are “forced to figure out how they want to interact with customers — and by customers, we mean Muse agents.”
  • This implies a need to redesign engagement strategies, though specific solutions were not detailed.

🤖 What Are Muse Agents?

  • The term Muse agents is used by the hosts to describe the AI‑powered entities that act as customers in this new shopping landscape.
  • No further definition or technical description was provided beyond the naming.

💭 Why It Matters

  • The discussion connects the AI shopping trend directly to broader questions about the future of the web and AI applications.
  • Understanding how Muse agents influence retail could become a focal point for future web and AI development conversations.

The Vergecast continues to invite listener feedback on these topics through their hotline and email.

#AIShopping #MuseAgents #RetailTech

Source: The iPhone Duo should have been an iPad

item.title: Walmart Denies Use of Personalized Pricing with Digital Shelf Labels
item.description:
Walmart Denies Use of Personalized Pricing with Digital Shelf Labels

Walmart has stated it will not use personal information or time of day to change product prices, following reports from The Wall Street Journal.

⚙️ Key details

In a letter to customers, CEO John Furner clarified the purpose and limitations of the company’s pricing strategies:

  • Digital Shelf Labels: The rollout of these labels in all US stores by the end of the year is intended to save store associates time, not to dynamically change prices.
  • Pricing Constraints: Prices will not be changed based on:
    • Personal income
    • Shopping history
    • Urgency
    • Perceived ability to pay
    • Time of day (e.g., a hot afternoon)
    • Sudden rushes for an item
  • AI Integration: Walmart will not use conversations with its Sparky AI assistant to change prices.

💡 Why it matters

The company’s reassurance comes amid increasing regulatory scrutiny:

  • Federal Level: The Federal Trade Commission is developing a policy to clamp down on personalized pricing.
  • State Level:
    • New York requires retailers to disclose the use of algorithmic pricing.
    • New Jersey, Connecticut, and Maryland have moved to ban the use of personal data to change store prices.

#Walmart #AI #PersonalizedPricing #RetailTech

Source: Walmart won’t hike prices based on your shopping history, CEO says
